messages:
Jordan: Thinking about collector topology — should we model a proxy hierarchy (local sidecar -> regional gateway -> central egress) to enable exporter fan-in and per-tenant retention tiers? Want pros/cons before I start a design doc.
Maria: +1 can you sketch the failure modes you care about? :thinking:
Lee: Main tradeoff: per-signal pipelines at the sidecar gives better isolation and earlier rejects, but syncing configs and policies across gateways becomes a pain.
Sasha: Also need to decide where quotas live — sidecar for low-latency local rejects vs gateway for global, consistent enforcement.
Tom: If we do exporter fan-in at the gateway we reduce outbound connections, but then the gateway needs to hold tenant creds and KMS access. Ops surface area increases.
infra-bot: Deploy-bot: snapshot created for canary 'collector-proxy-hierarchy' — CI build #4821.
Jordan: Quick config sketch for routing-by-header and retention tiers (very rough):
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
processors:
  tenant_routing:
    header: x-rw-tenant
exporters:
  gw_fan_in:
    endpoint: gw.region-1.redwood:4317
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [tenant_routing]
      exporters: [gw_fan_in]
```
Maria: Concern: batching + fan-in at gateway can increase tail latency (p99). We need benchmarks with realistic span sizes.
Lee: Proposal: route by tenant to gateway, enforce strict quotas at gateway using token-bucket (global view), sidecar keeps static local allotments to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Sasha: Also need Console surfaces: per-route latency heatmaps, dropped-by-quota counters, and a retention-tier view per tenant.
Tom: Rollout idea: mirror traffic to gateway (observe) for 2 weeks, then enable soft-rejects for a small canary tenant set, then hard reject. Keep a fallback path to bypass gateway.
Jordan: Agreed. I'll draft design doc and include compatibility notes (OTLP/HTTP), header auth, KMS integration, retention tiers, canary steps. Who wants to own the PoC?
Maria: I'll own the gateway fan-in PoC.
Lee: I'll handle sidecar quota behavior + e2e harness to simulate 10k tenants.
Sasha: I'll mock Console dashboards — need metrics: route_latency_ms, exporter_backpressure, dropped_by_quota.
Tom: Quick question: how to handle tenant-configured multiple exporters (fan-in -> fan-out)? Gateway streams to each destination async and applies backpressure per exporter so one slow third-party doesn’t block others.
Maria: Exactly. Gateway should spool and stream per-exporter with bounded buffers and per-exporter backoff.
Jordan: OK — next steps: create PoC board in #eng-platform, design doc PR from me by EOD Friday. Linking WIP notes: https://go/redwood/collector-proxy-hierarchy (WIP). :rocket:
Tom: +1. Thanks all.
